A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoGeR research and contain complete, readable main text and appendices A–B. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, camera-pose, depth, efficiency, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including revised VBR results in Figure 4 and Table 6.

M1.justification: Equation (10) adds the per-sequence scale s* to the predicted world-coordinate pointmap in the global loss, revising the stated training objective. The architecture and inference procedures remain unchanged; implementation changes or retraining are not established.

E1.justification: The training mixture and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including KITTI, VBR, 7-Scenes, ScanNet, TUM-Dynamics, Bonn, and qualitative scenes in the appendix.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments. The newly cited Longstream work is not added to any reported evaluation.

E3.justification: The stated ATE evaluation with Umeyama alignment, sequence selections, frame ranges, chunk/reset settings, and training schedules remain unchanged. The VBR score revisions are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: The TTT/SWA, training-data mixture, and curriculum ablations in Table 3 and Figure 10 are unchanged, as are the qualitative analyses and appendix efficiency evaluation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The revisions do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The central VBR results are substantially revised throughout Table 6 and Figure 4. Reported mean ATE changes from 5.40 to 36.16 m for LoGeR, 5.27 to 31.75 m for LoGeR*, and 7.62 to 70.81 m for TTT3R. Rankings also change: Pi3-Chunk now beats TTT3R on average. These are revised reported scores, not demonstrated changes in model capability; other benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (10) changes the mathematical definition of the global pointmap loss by multiplying the predicted global coordinates by s*. This is non-equivalent to the earlier formula; other definitions and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens the quantitative VBR improvement claim from 30.8% to 55.2%, matching the revised results. The main contributions, architectural claims, and claimed generalization scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of local consistency, global scale anchoring, and accumulated drift are retained. Limitations concerning effective memory length, periodic resets, and training-data availability are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, data processing, and the project-access link remain unchanged. Appendix A contains no revised reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Cheng et al. (2026), Longstream, among causal-attention approaches. A local CUT3R citation is removed from the TTT3R description, while that work remains cited elsewhere. Broader positioning is retained.

P1.justification: There are limited acknowledgment and citation-context edits, including thanking Zihan Zhu for VBR evaluation feedback, plus the updated version/date stamp. Section organization and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with revised ATE and input-view ticks, a relocated legend, and changed proportions that reflow nearby text. Table 6 retains its structure, and the remaining figures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The explicit scale factor in Equation (10) and added related-work citation offer limited clarity and attribution benefits. However, the substantial VBR revisions in Figure 4 and Table 6 lack an explanation of their cause, so the PDFs do not establish that the revised estimates are more valid. The larger reported relative gain alone does not resolve this uncertainty about overall quality.
